newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks see buying ahead of export data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks see buying ahead of export data.

text.p: Singapore stocks were mostly firmer at midday on Monday, underpinned by hopes of a supportive June non-oil export data, expected to be announced in the afternoon, dealers said.
"Sentiment is fairly stable. There is continued strength in some penny stocks on the perception that downside is limited. Interest in blue chips is still on a highly selective basis," said a dealer.
At 0430 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 9.64 points at 1,933.87. Total market turnover was about 113 million shares with 191 gainers to 117 losers.

AsiaMatrix Ltd dominated the actives, with over 14.7 million shares traded, fueled a proposed takeover bid for the plastics injection maker. Its shares hit a new 1997 high of Singapore $1.70 before easing to S$1.58 at lunch break.
The foreign tranch of DBS Bank gained 50 cents to S$19.60 on reports of its potential paper gains from a commercial property development in central Hong Kong.
